snip.t: Peripheral vascular disease (PVD) refers to conditions affecting blood circulation outside of the heart and brain, primarily involving the arteries and veins of the limbs.
Gangrenous necrosis is a typical complication of diabetes mellitus with marked peripheral vascular disease from atherosclerosis.

Proceed to hypertension and hypertensive emergencies, then heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, valvular disease and murmurs, infective endocarditis, ECG and arrhythmias, pericardial disease, cardiomyopathy, peripheral vascular disease and shock.
snip.s: Approach to Cardiovascular Symptoms and Examination

snip.t: *After completing this section, you will be able to approach a patient with suspected peripheral vascular disease in the Kenyan context, understanding its causes, presentation, examination, and initial investigations.

Comorbidities: HIV status, diabetes, sickle‑cell disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic steroid use, recent TB treatment, malaria, rheumatic disease — Immunocompromise or vascular disease predisposes to atypical organisms and poorer outcomes
Terlipressin: contraindicated in uncontrolled cardiac disease, active coronary ischemia, severe peripheral vascular disease.
Peripheral pulses & edema: Check for peripheral vascular disease, fluid overload — Hypertension and dyslipidaemia predispose to atherosclerosis; heart failure may cause edema.
